evidence_quotes.quote: This largely qualitative study used purposive sampling to select 104 women
There was no reasonable accommodation of women with disabilities who
disproportionately affected by limited access to water, sanitation, and hygiene

rationale: This qualitative study (structured interviews and focus group discussions with 104 purposively sampled women with disabilities plus 7 key informant interviews, analyzed thematically with simple descriptive statistics) examines barriers to WASH access in three low-income areas of Harare during COVID-19. Among rule- and governance-type mechanisms, the central empirical focus is discretion_accommodation: the failure to implement statutory/policy mandates for reasonable accommodation at communal water points and under COVID-19 restrictions, alongside informal/corrupt street-level queue gatekeeping by 'borehole marshals' demanding bribes or transactional sex to skip 3-6 hour queues (with secondary discussion of COVID-19 curfew enforcement by police and exclusion from participatory WASH planning and social assistance). The primary outcome is effective_access, encompassing physical accessibility of boreholes and wells, water-fetching burden and queue waiting/safety, water quantity and reliability, sanitation/waste disposal, and menstrual hygiene management (with secondary discussion of costs paid to neighbours or water carriers).
